traits.rosette.note: APweb, Nymphaeales page (read 2026-10-16): long internodes, floating stems.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: APweb, Nymphaeales page (read 2026-10-16): Cabomba (5 spp.) submerged leaves opposite or whorled; floating leaves and Brasenia spiral.

traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Cabombaceae: leaves alternate or opposite; leaves simple or compound; stipules absent; plants hermaphrodite; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems herbaceous; flowers solitary; perianth sepals and petals; fruit follicle; parts of each whorl 3; stamens 3 to 18; carpels (2-) 3 to 18. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 193, family Cabombaceae: leaf incision none or dissected (undivided floating leaves; submersed leaves divided into many segments), usually; read as {"dissected": "often", "none": "often"}.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 193, family Cabombaceae: flower symmetry actinomorphic; read as "actinomorphic".

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 193, family Cabombaceae: rhizome habit long_creeping (rhizomes give rise to elongate leafy shoots), usually; read as {"long_creeping": "usually"}.

traits.perennation.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Cabombaceae: how its perennial herbs last from year to year (character 25), coded usually a rhizome. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 25 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: APweb, Nymphaeales page, Cabombaceae (read 2026-10-16): Cabomba (about 7 of 8 species) has submerged leaves opposite or in whorls of three, while the peltate floating leaves (all of Brasenia's) are spiral; so opposite usually, whorled sometimes, alternate rarely (rarely rather than the proposed sometimes, since only one species relies on them).
